To: Renters Board / Notices
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Urgent: check your Brightline Pro 6% developer — batch LX2291

Hi everyone,

Please check your Brightline Pro 6% (20 vol) Cream Developer 1L before using it on anyone. Kelvin Trade has said a filling error means bottles from batch LX2291 may contain 12% (40 vol) developer, even though they’re labelled 6%.

Stop using any bottle with batch code LX2291 immediately. Kelvin says this batch was supplied between 19 October and 5 November 2026. They’ve said other batches and other strengths aren’t affected.

The batch code is on the BASE OF THE BOTTLE, not on the box. Please check every bottle individually, including any open ones in your trolley as well as the stock in the back. Don’t just check the box or assume an opened bottle is fine because you’ve already used it.

I used a new bottle from this batch on Saturday for a bleach retouch. The hair lifted much faster than usual and my client felt burning on her scalp. I rinsed it straight away, but she was left with a red, sore patch. Aileen has also checked her bottle and found it was LX2291 after her client’s foils got very hot on Thursday. The hair lifted unusually fast and ended up brassy and patchy.

Please be alert to faster-than-expected lift, excessive heat, burning or discomfort. A stronger developer can cause scalp injury as well as uneven or unwanted lift and damage to the hair. Don’t wait for any of these signs before checking your bottles.

If someone reacts in the chair and you suspect a chemical burn:

- Stop the service immediately. Put on gloves and carefully remove any contaminated clothing if possible.
- Call 999 for medical help immediately. Don’t wait for blisters or severe pain. Tell the call handler what’s happened and follow their instructions.
- Rinse the affected area with plenty of cool or lukewarm running water for about an hour. Don’t use shampoo, creams or other chemicals.
- Chemical burns need hospital assessment. Breathing difficulty, throat swelling or collapse also need an immediate 999 call.
- Record what happened in the incident book at the desk.

If you’ve had a problem, keep the bottle involved somewhere safe and clearly marked — don’t bin it. Keep a note of the batch, what was used and what happened, along with any photos and relevant records.

Kelvin Trade says affected bottles can be returned to the rep or taken to the Hillington depot for a full credit. The rep is in Tuesday. If a bottle was involved in an incident, keep it back rather than handing it over straight away, so it’s available for any investigation or insurance claim.

Please check today and pass this on to anyone else who might have bought it from the rep.

Kirsty

reasons: The line about keeping the bottle 'for any investigation or insurance claim' hints at the private insurance note (d05), which says to keep the bottle for the insurer.
